{"world_model":"W5 (contrarian), after E043. The tip is E036 (5.314 s). New fact the committee is missing: E043 ran the same commit (60645dd) with no recipe change, and seeds 0–2 came in at 0.7497. The three readings of E036's commit are now 0.7532 (E036), 0.7525 (E038) and 0.7497 (E043).

1. Rebuild nondeterminism is a noise source of the same size as seed noise. max-autotune and cuDNN benchmark pick kernels per build. Different reduction orders then make fp16/bf16 trajectories diverge chaotically, so the same seeds give a new draw on every build. E035's "math-identical" +0.09 pp and E043's −0.35 pp come from the same mechanism. So:
   - The 3-seed gate on a fresh build has an SD of about 0.15–0.2 pp, not the ~0.15 assumed for seed-only noise.
   - E036's population mean is probably about 0.752, below the 0.753 gate. Every keep since E033 was partly a lucky rebuild draw (winner's curse at the build level, not just the seed level).
   - Consequence: any change that leaves accuracy alone passes the gate only about 30–40% of the time. To clear the gate reliably, a cut needs about +0.1 pp of real accuracy behind it.
2. Exchange-rate frontier (kept): every trim (E033, E037, E039, E040, E041, E031) costs about 0.07–0.1 pp per 0.1 s. Mechanism: accuracy tracks the useful update signal, i.e. the share of steps × the share of the network those steps reach. Only pure overhead sits off the frontier.
3. E042 (0.7549) and E043 (0.7497) are both within ±1.5σ of the same population mean of about 0.752. I should widen my accuracy ranges and centre them near 0.752, not 0.7532.
4. Time is reproducible to about ±0.02 s and well predicted by pixel and step accounting. The stem-truncation savings are bandwidth-heavy. Group 2 is compute-bound and is the main feature block, so freezing it costs real signal.
5. BN calibration after the Lookahead copy is the remaining lever that leaves the trajectory unchanged. The lerped BN buffers mismatch the averaged weights (alpha reaches about 0.77 per update at the end). I expect +0.05–0.15 pp, and the paired offline design measures it cleanly. On the gate it is still swamped by rebuild noise.
6. Batch/steps (H5): splitting the 20 px phase into more steps pays roughly 3–4 ms of fixed overhead per step (Muon NS, Python loop, Lookahead). The gain is uncertain, so this likely lands on the frontier at best.
7. Systems: I expect Cin=24 padding to be close to neutral, because cuDNN already pads channels_last fp16 internally and the padding adds GELU and memory traffic at 31×31. I expect conv1 to be well under 10% of the full step's time.

Strategy: get variance down before cutting further. Average 2–3 builds per evaluation, or pin kernel choices (save the autotune cache) so seeds 0–2 become deterministic. Then pair the BN recalibration with one cut of about −0.1 s.

W5 (contrarian), after E043. The tip is E036 (5.314 s). New fact the committee is missing: E043 ran the same commit (60645dd) with no recipe change, and seeds 0–2 came in at 0.7497. The three readings of E036's commit are now 0.7532 (E036), 0.7525 (E038) and 0.7497 (E043).

1. Rebuild nondeterminism is a noise source of the same size as seed noise. max-autotune and cuDNN benchmark pick kernels per build. Different reduction orders then make fp16/bf16 trajectories diverge chaotically, so the same seeds give a new draw on every build. E035's "math-identical" +0.09 pp and E043's −0.35 pp come from the same mechanism. So:
   - The 3-seed gate on a fresh build has an SD of about 0.15–0.2 pp, not the ~0.15 assumed for seed-only noise.
   - E036's population mean is probably about 0.752, below the 0.753 gate. Every keep since E033 was partly a lucky rebuild draw (winner's curse at the build level, not just the seed level).
   - Consequence: any change that leaves accuracy alone passes the gate only about 30–40% of the time. To clear the gate reliably, a cut needs about +0.1 pp of real accuracy behind it.
2. Exchange-rate frontier (kept): every trim (E033, E037, E039, E040, E041, E031) costs about 0.07–0.1 pp per 0.1 s. Mechanism: accuracy tracks the useful update signal, i.e. the share of steps × the share of the network those steps reach. Only pure overhead sits off the frontier.
3. E042 (0.7549) and E043 (0.7497) are both within ±1.5σ of the same population mean of about 0.752. I should widen my accuracy ranges and centre them near 0.752, not 0.7532.
4. Time is reproducible to about ±0.02 s and well predicted by pixel and step accounting. The stem-truncation savings are bandwidth-heavy. Group 2 is compute-bound and is the main feature block, so freezing it costs real signal.
5. BN calibration after the Lookahead copy is the remaining lever that leaves the trajectory unchanged. The lerped BN buffers mismatch the averaged weights (alpha reaches about 0.77 per update at the end). I expect +0.05–0.15 pp, and the paired offline design measures it cleanly. On the gate it is still swamped by rebuild noise.
6. Batch/steps (H5): splitting the 20 px phase into more steps pays roughly 3–4 ms of fixed overhead per step (Muon NS, Python loop, Lookahead). The gain is uncertain, so this likely lands on the frontier at best.
7. Systems: I expect Cin=24 padding to be close to neutral, because cuDNN already pads channels_last fp16 internally and the padding adds GELU and memory traffic at 31×31. I expect conv1 to be well under 10% of the full step's time.

Strategy: get variance down before cutting further. Average 2–3 builds per evaluation, or pin kernel choices (save the autotune cache) so seeds 0–2 become deterministic. Then pair the BN recalibration with one cut of about −0.1 s.

Unsure: whether the E038 figure is from seeds 0–2 or 13–22; how the PCIe judge discounts bandwidth-bound levers; whether a recalibration on augmented train-mode batches could hurt.

forecasts.reason: The paired offline gain is likely +0.05–0.12 pp, under the ≥0.15 bar. The gate reading is dominated by rebuild noise.
About 69 extra steps × 3–4 ms of overhead adds about 0.25 s. The gain of maybe +0.1 pp sits on the frontier, not off it.
Group 2 is compute-bound and the main feature block. The saving is about −0.17 s but costs about 0.2 pp, consistent with the frontier and above the 0.1 pp budget.
With no recipe change, accuracy is just a rebuild re-roll near 0.752. I expect conv1 to be well under 10% of full-step time, despite its lower TFLOP/s.
A 5% step cut via selection is about −0.25 s for about −0.12 pp, roughly the frontier rate; the 20-seed test can't separate it from the 0.1 pp budget.
cuDNN already pads channels internally, and the extra GELU/memory traffic at 31×31 offsets any gain, so it falls short of −2%. Accuracy is a rebuild re-roll.

cruxes: How much of the seeds 0–2 variance comes from rebuilding with different kernels? E036/E038/E043 read 0.7532/0.7525/0.7497 on the same commit. Is E036's population mean about 0.752, below the gate, and can a pinned autotune cache make seeds 0–2 deterministic?
Does post-Lookahead BN recalibration give a paired gain of at least 0.1 pp? That is the only remaining lever that leaves the trajectory unchanged and could fund a cut of about 0.1 s.

Is any remaining time lever off the ~0.08 pp per 0.1 s frontier, i.e. pure overhead such as Python loop, Muon NS or per-epoch augmentation/interpolate time outside the graphs, as I071's whole-train trace would show?
